Community Overview
Emanuel in the Community
All pupils at Emanuel School are encouraged to be outward looking, to contribute to the community, whether local or global, to learn compassion and respect for others around them and to look outside their own needs. The school aims to foster aspiration and social mobility through education so that all young people in our local community, regardless of circumstances, are able to make the best of themselves.
We work collaboratively with 30 local state primary and secondary schools. Our partner schools are located within easy reach of Emanuel School and are prioritised based on the proportion of pupils on free school meals. We undertake a range of activities including programmes such as Primary Ambitions, DJing Classes and Ascent. Our pupils are involved in many of these activities – from support through to delivery of programme content.
In addition, we share our resources including our much-coveted swimming pool and mini-Astro. We organise weekly swimming lessons for local schools during term time. We host weekly disability football and hockey sessions facilitated by our partners Fulham Football Club Foundation and Wayfarer’s Flyerz. Our biodiversity garden is a wonderful new addition to our site and is a fantastic resource for our local schools too. Many of our pupils volunteer as part of their Duke of Edinburgh, an extremely popular programme, to support our community partners.
In addition, we support a range of charities that are chosen annually by our student body. Charities are both local and global enabling us to raise awareness about critical issues such as homelessness, as well as raise much needed funds. We assemble Christmas hampers for local single parent families in partnership with CHEER, a local charity, annually. We support Ace of Clubs, a homeless charity with food and coat donations and organise drives for technology, books, coats and, more recently, essential supplies for Afghan and Ukrainian refugees.
Our community partnership and outreach programme is wide ranging and is only possible through the support of our pupils, staff, parents and alumni.
If you would like to find out more, please contact Hannah Weatherhead, Community Partnerships and Outreach Coordinator at community@emanuel.org.uk

History of Emanuel
On 20th December 1594, the will of Lady Anne Dacre directed her executors to build “a meet and convenient house to be called Emanuel Hospital in Westminster for the relief of twenty aged people and for the bringing up of twenty children in virtue and good and laudable arts”.
This original bequest of £300 was the foundation of an education for 10 boys and 10 girls.
Emanuel Hospital, Westminster, pictured in the 19th century.
On 17th December 1601 Queen Elizabeth I, cousin to Lady Dacre, granted a Charter of Incorporation to the executors of Emanuel Hospital, but it was not until 1736 when children first benefited from the education. By the middle of the 19th century the school had expanded to 60 children, aged between 7 and 14. Due to the demand for education, the Endowed Schools Commission merged several school charities. Emanuel School rose from the ashes of Emanuel Hospital and the new institution relocated to Wandsworth. The girls who attended the old hospital school were sent to Grey Coat Hospital and Emanuel remained boys-only until 1995.
Opening at its present site in Wandsworth on 22nd January 1883, Emanuel School occupied a building which had formerly been the Royal Patriotic Asylum; an orphanage for boys. The initial school roll was around 200 pupils. Many of the original pupils were boarders, but as industrial London expanded, their numbers declined and eventually ceased in 1913.
HRM Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother on her visit to Emanuel School in 1951.
Over the 20th century Emanuel School slowly grew from a solitary building to the modern complex which now houses close to 1,000 pupils.
During the course of the First and Second World Wars, over 1,900 Old Emanuels (OEs) fought for their country with over 250 losing their lives. During the Second World War, the school was evacuated to the Hampshire town of Petersfield. HRM Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother visited Emanuel School in 1951, and subsequently, HRM Queen Elizabeth II was the guest of honour in 1994, leading the celebrations of the school’s 400th anniversary.
HRM Queen Elizabeth II, leading the celebrations of the school's 400th anniversary in 1994.
Between 1879 and 1944 the school charged fees, although many pupils were on scholarships. In 1944 Emanuel became a voluntary aided grammar school until 1976. Rather than become a comprehensive at this time, the school instead became an independent school – a status it maintains today. In the mid-1990s girls were admitted for the first time since 1882 and now, over 35 years later, the co-educational pupil population is close to equal numbers of boys and girls, just as the founder, Lady Dacre, intended.
The school chapel, 1900 (approx). Much of the chapel, located at the heart of the Victorian building, remains unchanged to this day.

Safeguarding
Emanuel School is committed to safeguarding the welfare of children in our care. We seek to do this by providing a caring, positive, safe and stimulating environment which promotes the social, physical and moral development of each pupil in the school, taking into account the child’s age, characteristics and needs.
We are determined to take all reasonable measures to address concerns about pupil welfare and to ensure that risks of harm to children’s welfare are minimised. To this end, we are committed to ensuring good levels of communication between staff, pupils, parents, agencies, police and support services provided by statutory and voluntary agencies, including Social Services. We recognise that confidentiality must wherever possible be respected in all matters relating to child protection.
We carry out checks on all staff, including references from previous employers, verification of identity and qualifications and a satisfactory disclosure from the Disclosure and Barring Service, before they take up an appointment in order to comply with existing legislation and guidance. We have procedures to deal with allegations made against staff. The school has a small team of teachers with designated child protection and safeguarding responsibilities. These include making contact with Social Services should there be a significant concern, and monitoring children known or thought to be at risk of harm. Members of our governing body have also been trained in child protection issues, and the Chair of Governors is the link governor in this area. A regular review of policies and procedures is undertaken to take account of changes in personnel and legislation and to monitor how the school’s duties have been discharged.
Pupils and the educational experience
We want Emanuel to be a safe school. Children have a number of staff to whom they can turn when they need advice and support, e.g. form teachers, the teachers with designated child protection responsibilities, school counsellors and the chaplain.
We have created a curriculum which fosters the personal, emotional and social development of every pupil. The life education programme considers issues of personal safety and health. The school in no way condones bullying or racist incidents; guidance is issued to staff in these areas, and life education lessons cover these issues.
Our health and safety policy reflects the consideration we give to the protection of our children both within the school environment and when undertaking trips and visits away from school. We promote security on school sites through security staff and staff duties in the school.
The Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy is available to read on the policies page here.
If you have any specific pastoral or safeguarding concerns, we encourage you to contact the school’s designated safeguarding lead, Mrs McIsaac (Deputy Head: Pupils) or any member of the school’s safeguarding team (safeguarding@emanuel.org.uk)

Emanuel is part of Operation Encompass, a national scheme that operates jointly between schools and police forces.
Operation Encompass reports to schools, prior to the start of the next school day, when a child or young person has experienced domestic abuse. The Domestic Abuse Act 2021 identifies children who experience domestic abuse as victims of domestic abuse in their own right. Operation Encompass has now passed into law and places a statutory obligation on police forces to share notifications with the school.
Members of our safeguarding staff have been trained in the Operation Encompass procedures allowing us to then use the information that has been shared, in confidence, to support any child in our care.

Welcome to Admissions
We have four entry points at Emanuel: Year 6 (10+), Year 7 (11+), Year 9 (13+) and Sixth Form (16+).
We welcome applications from young people who want to work hard, throw themselves into the opportunities of independent school life and become responsible members of their communities.
On occasion we are able to offer an occasional place in years 8, 9 or 10 if any become available, read more here.
Our admissions process is designed to help us assess if each candidate will flourish both academically and holistically in the school. It is important to us that the pupils we offer places to will make the most of their time here and gain the most from the educational experience. While we value academic ability, we are also interested in pupils who display talent in other areas.
Open Events
Prospective parents and pupils are encouraged to find out more about the school from our online materials and by attending a school open event. Learn more about open events. Sign up to our mailing list to be the first to find out about our key dates and open events.
Subscribe to Admissions Mailing List
Be the first to receive updates from the admissions department
Prospectus
At Emanuel, we combine a long and proud tradition of academic and co-curricular success with a clear, forward-looking vision: to foster aspiration, connection and empathy in every pupil. Our Year 6 and Year 7 entry prospectus includes information on admissions, fees and scholarships.
Siblings
Priority is given to the siblings of existing pupils at the school who are applying to enter the school in Year 6 or Year 7 OR at the proposed time of entry, although admission is not automatic and the applicant must meet the admissions criteria set out in the Admissions Policy.
Admissions Policy
Emanuel School is a co-educational day school for pupils aged 10 – 19 years. The main entry points into the school are at Year 6 (10+), Year 7 (11+) and Sixth Form (16+). The school does not routinely admit pupils at other entry points, although will consider applicants for occasional vacancies into Years 8, 9 and 10 if places become available.
For more detailed information, please see our Admissions Policy and Admissions related Frequently Asked Questions.

Facilities and Development
Our school is located on a beautiful, leafy 12-acre site in Battersea, on the north edge of Wandsworth Common.
Its fantastic position, only 10 minutes’ walk from Clapham Junction rail station, connects the school to the hub of central London, as well as north and south of the river. Learn more about travelling to Emanuel School here. Read more about our facilities and development projects below.
The handsome Victorian building at the centre of the school site was originally designed by noted architect Henry Saxon Snell (1831-1904) as the Royal Victoria Patriotic School, funded by the Royal Patriotic Fund for children orphaned during the Crimean War. At its heart is a peaceful, ornate chapel, a wonderful library with a well-stocked archive and the tranquil Queens’ courtyard, named after Queen Elizabeth I, Queen Elizabeth II and Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother.
The school has the feel of a green oasis.
The Dacre building, named after the school's founder, Lady Anne Dacre, was opened in September 2017. The Dacre building is home to the creative arts.
We have always aimed to provide our pupils with the best educational environment. In the last 15 years, we have built a state-of-the-art theatre and professional film studio, well-resourced science laboratories, computing, coding and design suites and a sports hall and fitness centre.
In 2017, modern and spacious classrooms and colourful, bright and airy art studios were created with the opening of the new Dacre building. In 2018, the original Victorian building, including the reception, corridors and many classrooms, underwent significant stylistic renovations.
We have exceptional sports facilities on-site, including a large sports hall, a mini-astro, an indoor swimming pool and playing fields, as well as an all weather pitch for hockey and grass pitches for rugby, football and cricket at our offsite sports ground, Blagdons, near Raynes Park. We also have the use of off-site facilities, including Barnes Hockey Club and All Stars Tennis. Find out more about our sports facilities here.
We intend to sustain the development of our classroom and teaching facilities in the years to come with our site masterplan. Find out more about upcoming site projects here.

Travelling to Emanuel
Emanuel School is particularly well connected.
There are various modes of transport that service the local area, with Clapham Junction Rail Station a 10-minute walk away. All South Western Railway services to and from London Waterloo pass through Clapham Junction, as do trains with Southern Rail, the Gatwick Express and some trains in the London Overground network. The closest London Underground station to the school is Clapham Common, which is accessible via the 35 or 37 bus.
Our closest bus stops are on the 77 route (Waterloo Station to Tooting Station) and the 219 route (Clapham Junction to Wimbledon), with stops situated on Spencer Park/Battersea Rise. There are many more bus routes accessible within a short walk of the school. Please visit Transport for London for full transport details or to plan a route to Emanuel School. The map below shows the school’s connections to areas of London and approximate travel time from each station to Clapham Junction.
Our Sustainable Travel Policy
We are working closely with Transport For London to promote safe, active, responsible and sustainable travel (STARS) and have developed the following sustainable travel policy where we encourage pupils, parents and staff to travel actively to school by walking, cycling and scooting wherever possible. Read more here.
Parking
Visitor parking, including the parking area by the astroturf pitch, is currently unavailable. A temporary disabled parking bay for a single Blue Badge holder will be designated at the entrance to the driveway.
There are parking bays on several streets nearby, especially in Spencer Park and Chivalry Road. To access the school, please enter via the road bridge on Spencer Park (postcode SW18 2SZ).

Visiting Emanuel School
The sections on this page and in the visitor information leaflet are provided to help you before your arrival and during your visit at Emanuel School, including how to arrive at the school in Battersea, our safeguarding protocols, visiting procedures, accessibility, sporting fixture attendance, and photography and mobile phone usage.
Travelling to Emanuel
Emanuel School is particularly well connected with various modes of transport that service the local area, including Clapham Junction Rail Station a 10-minute walk away and various bus routes at a short walking distance. Read transport options here. We are working closely with Transport For London to promote safe, active, responsible and sustainable travel (STARS) and have developed the following sustainable travel policy where we encourage pupils, parents and staff to travel actively to school by walking, cycling and scooting wherever possible.

Welcome from the headmaster
I am delighted to welcome you to Emanuel.
We are a warm, ambitious and forward-looking school where pupils are encouraged to aim high, support one another and make a meaningful contribution to the world around them. We are proud to be a thriving co-educational day school, where aspiration, connection and empathy are central to everything we do.
Our pupils strive for excellence not only in the classroom, but also in the many creative, sporting and social opportunities that are part of daily school life. Whether on stage, on the pitch, in a lab or in a leadership role, they are supported by passionate, expert teachers who care deeply about their subjects – and even more about inspiring the young people they teach. It is this trusted relationship between pupils, teachers and families that lies at the heart of our success.
We believe that education is about much more than results. We want our pupils to feel known and valued for who they are, and to develop confidence, kindness and resilience as they grow. Through our outstanding pastoral care, pupils are encouraged to be thoughtful, reflective and inclusive – qualities we believe are just as important as academic achievement.
Our vibrant co-curricular programme provides countless opportunities for pupils to challenge themselves, discover new interests and feel part of something bigger than themselves – whether that’s a house team, music ensemble, sports team or one of our many pupil-led clubs and societies. Emanuel is a busy school by design: we know that young people thrive when they are actively involved, learning to lead, collaborate and celebrate one another’s successes.
This sense of responsibility to others extends beyond the school gates. Through our award-winning partnerships and outreach work, pupils learn the value of giving back and begin to understand the positive impact they can have on the wider world.
We are ambitious for the future. In 2025, we began work on a transformational new STEM and Refectory building – set to open in 2027 – which will provide state-of-the-art science laboratories, collaborative teaching spaces and a new dining facility. This follows recent investments in a new Sixth Form Centre, all-weather Astro, new cricket and netball facilities and more – each project shaped by our commitment to delivering a dynamic, inclusive education that equips pupils for the changing world.
We are incredibly proud of Emanuel’s rich heritage, inclusive ethos and the energy and warmth of our community. I encourage you to come and visit us at one of our open events and experience the school for yourself.

About Emanuel School
Welcome to Emanuel School
Emanuel School is an independent co-educational day school for pupils aged 10–18, based in Battersea, London. It prides itself on a nurturing, respectful, and inclusive community anchored in Christian values, where teaching, pastoral care, and co-curricular life are all designed to develop “happy, confident, and kind” young people with high aspirations.
The school offers a broad, rigorous academic curriculum — from foundational subjects in younger years through a wide A-level choice — supported by strong pastoral support and a commitment to equity and diversity. With outstanding facilities, flourishing arts and sports programmes, and a strong outreach ethos, Emanuel seeks to prepare students for both academic success and meaningful contribution to their communities.
Welcome from the Headmaster
We are a warm, ambitious and forward-looking school where pupils are encouraged to aim high, support one another and make a meaningful contribution to the world around them. We are proud to be a thriving co-educational day school, where aspiration, connection and empathy are central to everything we do.
Facilities and Development
Our school is located on a beautiful, leafy 12-acre site in Battersea, on the north edge of Wandsworth Common. We have always aimed to provide our pupils with the best educational environment. In the last 15 years, we have built a state-of-the-art theatre and professional film studio, well-resourced science laboratories, computing, coding and design suites and a sports hall and fitness centre. Click here to learn more.
ISI Inspection Report
The ISI report at Emanuel School met all inspection standards across every area of school life. The report paints a compelling picture of a school community defined by kindness and purpose, where pupils are confident, motivated, and deeply engaged in their learning.

Working at Emanuel
The words that most of our staff associate with our school are “friendly”, “welcoming” and “caring”.
It is this warm culture that people comment on when they visit the school, and it’s a significant reason for the school’s popularity with parents and the local community. Within this supportive environment, it’s no wonder that pupils thrive and are enabled to achieve their best academic potential, as well as developing specialist skills in art and design, drama, music and sport.
The staff team at Emanuel embody the words above – everyone works hard here, and anyone joining the school should expect to be kept busy, but there’s a strong sense of community and friendship. There is also a genuine ongoing dialogue about what the school is up to, and where it’s headed, with a weekly staff briefing, half-termly staff meetings, termly consultative group meetings and dynamic common room committee.
We work hard to look after all our staff and support their development and wellbeing: our appraisal scheme focuses on each individual employee’s professional development; we sponsor postgraduate courses and a range of training opportunities; we offer a healthcare plan via Simply Health that includes counselling and support. All staff benefit from good pension provision and free lunch – which is always excellent.
Classrooms are well resourced. All teaching staff have their own tablets and our ICT facilities are regularly upgraded to support the latest teaching initiatives. Our friendly and well-behaved pupils respond to caring and dynamic teaching and, as an independent school, there is the freedom to teach to your strengths and try out new approaches. Class sizes are normally no more than 24 pupils and often much smaller for GCSE and A Level groups, so teaching staff have time and space to help individuals and concentrate on effective teaching.
If you’re interested in joining our staff team, then please review the job vacancies and information packs. They will give you a good flavour of the different roles and departments that you will be applying to. We are looking for excellent, motivated teaching and support staff, who are excited about playing their part in our school’s development. I hope that you will want to join us.
Sarah Buxton Director of HR
